verdict.tagline: Open roads and heavy loads offer a relaxing drive across Europe.
for_you_if: you want a relaxing driving experience
you enjoy listening to podcasts while playing
you use a steering wheel or controller
not_for_you_if: you only play with a keyboard and mouse
you expect modern multi-threaded engine performance
you are bothered by poor traffic artificial intelligence

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Long-term players praise the relaxing pace but point out outdated engine limitations, poor traffic behavior, and aging base map regions.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that traffic AI behavior is poor and lacks intelligence, negatively impacting immersion.

citations.review_text:
This game is the goat. Year after year I nominate it for Labor of Love award, it just never seems to win. But when I think back of the barebones low graphics and highly inconvenient gameplay PoS from 2013, the SCS team spent so much time making this game bigger and better it's unreal. 

Nowadays ETS2 and ATS are my favorite relaxed games. It's like the miniature wonderland you dreamt of building in your basement some thirty years ago. But someone else build it for you and you can drive around in it for realsies. 

Of course there are still a few things I wished they would do better, and they work on too many projects at once so stuff takes literal years after the initial announcement to release. And ofc the number of DLC releases has almost turned this game into sort of a soft live-service, which is not always the most desirable outcome.

But honestly it's still worth playing ETS2 in 2027 for probably the best arcade simulation of anything, based on sheer size and accessibility.


ps.
[spoiler]The lack of intelligence in the traffic Ai is the bane of my existence.[/spoiler]

Euro Truck Simulator 2 is undoubtedly an expansive and atmospheric title, but there's no point in listing its pros – anyone interested already knows them well.

So why am I giving it a negative review? Because the developers have clearly shifted into blatant monetization mode, leaving the game's core foundations in ruins.

It's full of bugs. The AI traffic behavior is stuck at an embarrassingly poor level. The same flaws and broken AI patterns have dragged on for years, and no one at the studio wants to touch them. In a title that calls itself a "simulator," this severely ruins immersion and takes away any joy of driving.

ETS2 is an aging game. SCS knows full well how badly the oldest regions lag behind the latest DLCs in terms of quality. Yet, reworking the base map and older areas is moving at a snail's pace. Entering "legacy" DLCs like Going East! is painful – that map is a graphical and technical fossil today. When will they fix it? Who knows, because the studio preferred to divert manpower elsewhere – after all, new DLCs bring in money, while free reworks of old areas don't pay the bills.

On top of that, content is being shoved into the game forcefully and without any sense of direction. In ETS2, announcing coaches actually makes sense – they are large commercial vehicles that require new mechanics (bus stations, passengers, timetables) and fit the logic of transport. Meanwhile, in its sister game ATS, they added passenger cars and clearly don't even know why. Claiming it's for "sightseeing" is plain ridiculous – trucks were meant for taking in the views, not a Mustang. It just shows a total lack of a coherent vision and pushing filler content instead of patching the foundations.

To wrap it up, there's the studio's terrible hypocrisy and political inconsistency. When Russia attacked Ukraine, they instantly shelved the ready-to-release Heart of Russia DLC. But when the US conducts aggressive foreign policy, SCS turns a blind eye, pretends not to notice, and u…
very good! But be careful of the npcs because they do not know how to drive! good game tho!

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game engine is outdated and fails to utilize multiple CPU threads effectively.

citations.review_text:
Really good and suprisingly relaxing game where you can turn your brain off and just drive. SCS still continues to push updates and map expansions despite the game's age. Not the best if you want a real simulator, but still a great game to kick back and haul cargo across Europe.
Some minuses are that almost all updates are dlc's, outdated game engine that can't utualize the whole cpu and forgoten places of the map like Poland and the UK.

I enoy everything about this game since i started playing it including always expanding map, physics, great customization and playability especially with controller except one thing that cant arrive soon enough which is reworking of the game engine to use more than one CPU thread for carriying all the load. Yes you can see my specs and GPU and use of standard HDD is two weaker points but new one is getting built in due time. In saying that, not having my i9 9900k utilized by this game and ATS yet is a shame haha
